title: Solent Kestrels claim NBL1 Playoff title
description: Solent completed their league, cup and playoff treble with a hard-fought 74-66 victory against Worcester Wolves. In a fitting showpiece between the top-two D1M sides during the regular-season, Solent found a way to just edge ahead of a dogged opponent, as they have so many times in recent years. Drawing from across their deep roster to get themselves over the line, Solent's shared load was demonstrated by six different players contributing six or more points to the Kestrels' total, allowing the South coast programme to win their first D1M title since 2021/22. Solent's lead flirted with the 15-point mark in both the second and fourth quarter, but credit to the Wolves as they fought back on both occasions to threaten a mighty comeback. Coach Guymon's side would eventually shut the door on those plans, led by MVP Andre Arissol (188-G-1997, college: Chaminade) as he dropped a game-high 19…
imageCaption: Solent Kestrels claim NBL1 Playoff title (Photo: basketballengland.co.uk)

title: Hemel Storm top Reading Rockets to conquer NBL D1 playoff title
description: Reading R. - Hemel Storm 84-87 American guard Taylor Johnson (193-1994, college: Dartmouth) stepped up and scored 26 points, 5 rebounds and 4 assists for the winners and guard Sam Newman (191-1996) chipped in 18 points, 5 rebounds, 8 assists and 5 steals. Storm's coach Mark Clark used a ten-player rotation in such tough game. At the losing side Australian guard Mitchell Clarke (186-1999) responded with 16 points, 7 rebounds and 4 assists and American guard Elijah Maynard (193-1996, college: WAU) scored 15 points and 5 rebounds. Four Storm and five Rockets players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Hemel Storm top Reading Rockets to conquer NBL D1 playoff title (Photo: Instagram)

title: Hemel Storm outscore Worthing Thunder for NBL1 Playoff title
description: Hemel Storm became only the second team in the NBL's 50 year history to go undefeated across a full season and claim four trophies, sealing their quadruple in the Playoff Final with a 69-63 win over Worthing Thunder. Storm have swept past so many teams this season, including Worthing in a 126-73 thumping in the final game of the regular season, but Thunder stood tall throughout the contest to provide a fitting spectacle to end the season. Hemel were even restricted to a single-digit quarter (7pts) in the third, something that happened just once in the entire 2022/23 campaign, but the regular season champs responded to come out firing in the fourth, manufacturing a 12-2 run that created an advantage they'd never relinquish. MVP honours were shared between Hemel's Taylor Johnson (193-G-1994, college: Dartmouth) and Aaryn Rai (198-G/F, college: Dartmouth) in a first for the competition.…
imageCaption: Hemel Storm outscore Worthing Thunder for NBL1 Playoff title (Photo: basketballengland.co.uk)

title: Solent Kestrels celebrate NBL D1 title
description: Solent K. - Hemel Storm 71-69 Solent Kestrels held off Hemel Storm to celebrate NBL D1 title. Kestrels forced 20 Storm turnovers. Worth to mention a great performance of American guard Cole Gentry (178, college: Wright St.) who helped to win the game recording 19 points and 4 steals. The former international forward Orlan Jackman (201-1988, college: Okla City) contributed with 10 points and 7 rebounds for the winners. American guard Taylor Johnson (193-1994, college: Dartmouth) answered with 23 points, 8 rebounds and 7 assists and the other American import forward Gregory Poleon (199-1997, college: Pace) added 22 points and 14 rebounds in the effort for Storm.
imageCaption: Solent Kestrels celebrate NBL D1 title (Photo: hoopsfix.com)

title: Solent Kestrels win NBL Playoff title
description: Team Solent Kestrels added the 2020-21 NBL Playoff crown to the NBL league title and L Lynch Trophy already in their possession with a commanding final display in Manchester. Coach of the Year Matt Guymon guided his team to a convincing 93-62 victory over third seeds Hemel Storm at the National Basketball Performance Centre behind a stunning scoring effort from guard Ian Smith (178-PG-96, college: Northern St.). The game MVP racked up 37 points off 57% shooting - which included 7-12 from three-point range - dished out nine assists and took 11 rebounds as the Kestrels capped another highly successful campaign. Orlan Jackman (201-F-88, college: Okla City) backed him up with 18 (9rbs), while Travis Charles (198-F-95, college: Albany) had 13 (9rbs). imageCaption: Solent Kestrels win NBL Playoff title (Photo: basketballengland.co.uk)
